messages:
jake: noticed a 12-28ms tail latency bump on the small-chat path after yesterday's scheduler tweak. numbers from prod dashboards look noisy but consistent across regions.

maria: ugh. is this with kv-cache enabled?

jake: yes, only on requests with prefix caching (kv cache hit). pure cold KV runs look fine.

sam: can you paste the per-token breakdown?

jake: copied from trace sampler: 
```
model: redwood-flash-v2
route: chat.small
median_latency: 38ms -> 51ms (regression)
kv_apply: +6ms
attn_kernel_select: fused_flash -> fallback_gemm (around step 1)
batch_size: 1-2
```

rachel: that kernel flip is suspicious. maybe heuristics now prefer paged/flash fallback for short sequences?

jake: I ran a local reproduce with the same request shape. profiling shows GPU kernel time increased: fused flash path stays ~18ms but we end up on gemm fallback at ~32ms.

sam: any recent changes to kernel selection logic? I merged a micro-heuristics PR last night (hash: b7f4a1c).

maria: yeah that PR adjusted the batch-size cutoff to favor fused kernels for larger batches. might have inadvertently altered the warm-start decision for cached KV prefix.

amit: pinging perf-bot to run a bisect between main@b7f4a1c^ and main@b7f4a1c

perf-bot: bisect job queued: comparing main@b7f4a1c~1..main@b7f4a1c across 5 kube nodes. will post results. :hourglass: 

jake: meanwhile I ran a quick A/B locally toggling KV cache prefetch on/off. with prefetch disabled, kernel chooses fused_flash and tail latency drops back to baseline. with prefetch on, it hits fallback.

rachel: that suggests prefetch changes timing of KV availability and influences the kernel selection path. could be an interplay between scheduling and kernel-choice time window.

sam: can you share the scheduler trace? any batching boundary shifts?

jake: paste of scheduler slice (simplified):
```
[request_enqueue]
-> batch_collect (timeout 2ms)
-> kv_prefetch_fire (async)
-> kernel_choice (uses heuristics: available_kv, estimated_seq, batch_window)
-> dispatch
```
We see kernel_choice runs before kv_prefetch finishes about ~1.2ms of the time for cached hits, so heuristics think KV not ready and pick fallback.

maria: ok that's the root cause: ordering race. kernel_choice should be deferred or re-evaluated once kv_prefetch completes for cached prefixes.

amit: possible quick fix: add a cheap probe in kernel chooser to detect pending kv handles and stall if latency budget allows. or flip heuristics to bias toward fused when sequence length small.

sam: both have tradeoffs. stalling can add latency for truly cold paths. heuristic flip risks hurting heavy-batched workloads.

jake: I've got a micro-patch that defers kernel_choice by up to 0.8ms if kv_prefetch outstanding and batch_size <=2. locally it recovers median to 40ms. want to run canary.

rachel: +1 to canary. schedule on canary pool and include both kv-heavy and cold traffic.

ci-bot: canary deploy started: canary-12 -> cluster-canary-us-west (images: runtime:b7f4a1c+patch)

perf-bot: canary perf snapshot: baseline vs patch (5k samples each)
```
path: chat.small (kv-hit)
baseline median: 50.8ms
patch median: 39.6ms
p90: 78ms -> 55ms
kernel_select_distribution: fallback_gemm 82% -> 12%
```

sam: nice. what about cold KV and large-batch regressions?

perf-bot: cold-kv path (batch>=8): median 28ms -> 29ms (no significant impact).

maria: this looks promising. still want a cleaner fix in kernel chooser instead of ad-hoc delay. maybe allow kernel_choice to run but re-evaluate if kv arrives within X ms and selection favored fallback.

amit: another angle is to surface a fast kv-ready hint from cache layer synchronously when it has warm prefix metadata. that avoids waiting for full prefetch but informs chooser. cheaper than stall.

jake: agree. i'll prototype the kv-hint approach and revert the micro-delay after landing a proper hint.

rachel: created a follow-up ticket: PERF-2349 "kv-ready hint for kernel chooser" and assigned to jake+amit. add tests for small-batch kv-hit path.

sam: perf-bisect results from earlier bisect job: culprit commit b7f4a1c indeed widened batch_window default and changed ordering. revert portion improves numbers.

maria: thanks for quick triage. next steps: 1) keep canary running for 24h, 2) land kv-hint design, 3) add unit/integration tests around kernel_choice timing, 4) run broader perf suite across models.

jake: I'll post a short PR soon with the hint prototype.

rachel: awesome, please add a short note in the release notes about this behavioral tweak so on-call knows the root cause.

sam: and tag infra team if this needs any scheduler config changes.

jake: thanks all. I'll update thread with PR link and perf snapshots. :white_check_mark:
